name: Grundregeln für Gäste, die eine Unterkunft gebucht haben
text: Airbnb Help Center article 2894 (German; page date unknown, 2026-01-01 default) is the guest ground rules page, not the new host house rules policy. It states guests should leave the place without need for intensive or deep cleaning, that host cleaning fees only cover standard cleaning between stays, and that hosts may not charge fees for not completing certain cleaning tasks at checkout. It does not mention the 20 Nov 2026 policy or its effective date.

name: Wichtige Änderungen bei den Hausregeln (Airbnb Info-Center)
text: Airbnb primary page (German; undated, fetch metadata says 2026-10-20, but it refers back to the 20 Oct announcement so it is the later hosts' update, which Skift dates 3 Nov 2026). Airbnb says many hosts raised concerns about losing control and admits it should have explained the changes better. Tasks are renamed 'Zusätzliche Regeln' (additional rules). The policy takes effect 20 Nov 2026; first reviews then run until March 2027, afterwards listings are reviewed continuously. Non-compliant hosts are notified by email and in-app and get at least 20 days to update or appeal; one appeal only, with documents; if rejected and kept, guests may see a notice on the listing. Allowed: dishes in the sink, collect used towels, sort rubbish into building bins, switch off air-conditioning; not allowed: washing dishes, stripping beds, taking rubbish off-site, forgoing listed amenities. Exceptions possible (bears, drought). Hosts should generally not fine guests. Contracts only for few reasons (law, insurance, HOA, long-stay leases, Airbnb Luxe, optional equipment such as golf carts); Airbnb does not help enforce them. Seven standard rules incl. lock-up at checkout. Hosts can cancel penalty-free if guests break a house rule.

name: Airbnb Q3 2026 financial results
text: Airbnb newsroom, 5 Nov 2026 (primary): Q3 revenue +19% YoY to $4.9 billion, GBV +21% to $27.7 billion, nights and seats booked +16%, net income $1.9 billion, adjusted EBITDA +22% to $2.5 billion (52% margin). New authorization to repurchase up to an additional $12 billion of Class A stock. Q4 2026 revenue guided to $3.22 to $3.28 billion (+16% to 18%); FY2026 revenue growth now high teens, adjusted EBITDA margin about 36%. AI assistant resolved about 40% of support issues without a human (a third in Q2); own AI agent rollout planned for first half 2027. Redesigned multi-listing calendar: nearly 1 in 4 eligible hosts opted in during early access. Amex partnership launched 22 Oct; thousands of hotels in 60+ destinations.

name: Penertiban OTA Dorong 5.000 Villa di Bali Mengurus Legalitas Usaha
text: Balinetizen reports Koster told the DPRD Bali plenary on 21 Sep 2026 that 5,000 villa businesses applied for licences in 2025-2026 after OTAs stopped marketing unlicensed lodging; hotel occupancy at 80-90% daily. Background: on Friday 8 May 2026 at Jayasabha (Governor's residence) Koster gathered OTA operators and made two demands: list and market only legal tourism businesses, and help the government collect the Tourism Levy Bali, a charge on foreign tourists.

name: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force
text: BBC News (via Yahoo), 20 Nov 2026: the rules are in force. Hosts choose from seven standard rules, may add additional rules, but guests should not be asked to wash up, strip beds, take out rubbish or avoid using utilities. Airbnb has begun reviewing listings and emails hosts who must act; hosts can appeal; if a rule is not approved and kept, Airbnb flags it on the listing page with a message such as 'includes cleaning tasks'. Some hosts (Lisa Clewes, Welsh holiday let, four-hour cleaner turnaround) say extra cleaning costs may be passed on to guests; guest Jessica Newhook paid a $250 cleaning fee yet faced a long checkout list. Frustration among owners adds to Airbnb's commission increases last year; many invest in own websites for direct bookings. Matt Porsz is relaxed about the changes.

name: BFS Tourismus: Publikationsübersicht (HESTA-Flash Oktober, Parahotellerie Q3)
text: BFS Themenseite Tourismus, Stand 23.11.2026: listet die HESTA-Flash-Schätzungen (erste und zweite Schätzung Oktober 2026; erste Schätzung November und Dezember 2026) sowie die Publikation 'Parahotellerie im 3. Quartal 2026' (laut Suche 24.11.2026, Zahlen noch nicht lesbar) und Monetäre Tourismusindikatoren 2024-2025 (touristische Bruttowertschöpfung 2025 +1,5 Prozent, Hotellerie -0,5 Prozent). Die Seite nennt keine Oktober-Prozentwerte; diese stehen nur in den Agenturtexten. Die Parahotellerie-Seite nennt Q2 2026: 3,9 Mio. Logiernächte, kommerzielle Ferienwohnungen 985 000.

name: Schweizer Hotels zählen im Oktober mehr Logiernächte (erste Schätzung)
text: Keystone-SDA via Bluewin, 16.11.2026: Laut erster BFS-Schätzung stieg die Zahl der Hotel-Logiernächte im Oktober 2026 gegenüber dem Vorjahresmonat um 2,0 Prozent; ausländische Gäste +2,3 Prozent, inländische +1,6 Prozent. Januar bis September 2026: 34,5 Millionen Logiernächte, geringfügig weniger als im Vorjahreszeitraum; für den Jahresrekord 2025 braucht es einen guten Wintersaisonstart. Das BFS veröffentlicht am 23. November die zweite Schätzung mit ersten Herkunftsmärkten und am 7. Dezember die absoluten Zahlen für Oktober und die Sommersaison 2026. Wire text from Keystone-SDA (a different agency from cash's AWP).

name: Booking.com Research Reveals There's No Place Like (Someone Else's) Home for Christmas
text: Booking.com press release (18 Nov 2026), UK only. Opinium survey 9-16 Oct 2026 of 2,000 UK adults who celebrate Christmas: 15% plan to spend Christmas away from home; 16% cite enough beds and 14% cost splitting as reasons to rent a holiday home; 45% of 18-34s would rent a whole home. Booking.com search data: country-home searches by families +22% vs last December, farm stays +25% for groups (UK searches May-Nov 2026 for stays 24-27 Dec 2026); Ambleside +37%, Whitby +32%, Ko Lanta (Thailand) +117% year on year. No Switzerland/Germany figures and no hotel-vs-home comparison. Marketing content, low relevance.

name: Online rental platforms face tougher checks as EU data-sharing laws debut
text: Brussels Times, 21 May 2026: EU short-term rental transparency rules under Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 are now in force, applying in countries that opt in. Opt-in states must run fully online registration with a unique number per property. Platforms must display and verify numbers, run random checks, and share monthly data with authorities via each state's Single Digital Entry Point; authorities can order removal of non-compliant listings. Lighter rules for small and micro platforms; aggregated data feeds Eurostat. The Commission says STR is about a quarter of EU tourist accommodation offers; guests spent 951.6 million nights in platform-booked STR in 2025.

name: Basler Grosser Rat will Registrierungspflicht für Aibnb-Wohnungen
text: cash.ch (AWP), 23.09.2026: Gleiche Meldung wie htr (SDA). Die Motion Balmer verlangt, dass die Regierung eine Änderung der gesetzlichen Grundlagen vorlegt; Registrierung vor Aufnahme der Vermietung. Balmer verweist auf das diesjährige Bundesgerichtsurteil, das die Einschränkungen von Business-Apartments der Stadt Zürich stützt, und sagt, damit hätte man mindestens 1500 Wohnungen wieder beim normalen Mietmarkt. FDP (Barth) und LDP (Iselin) warnen vor Bürokratie und Generalverdacht, LDP-Grossrat Alex Ebi unterstützt die Motion. Stimmenzahl nennt cash nicht.

name: Schweizer Hotels zählen im Oktober mehr Logiernächte (zweite Schätzung)
text: AWP via cash.ch, 23.11.2026: Zweite BFS-Schätzung für Oktober 2026: Hotel-Logiernächte +1,9 Prozent zum Vorjahresmonat; ausländische Gäste +2,0 Prozent, einheimische +1,9 Prozent (erste Schätzung: +2,0 / +2,3 / +1,6). Europa +4,7 Prozent, Frankreich +11,3, Niederlande +6,6, UK +3,9, Deutschland +0,1, Italien +0,2. Amerika +6,8 Prozent, USA +4,0. Asien -7,9 Prozent: China -5,3, Indien +6,2, Golfstaaten +4,4. Januar bis September 34,5 Mio. Logiernächte, knapp unter Vorjahr; Rekord 2025 war 43,9 Mio. Absolute Zahlen für Oktober und Sommersaison 2026 am 7. Dezember. No regional (Zürich, Graubünden etc.) numbers in the text.

name: Resmi! UMP Bali 2027 Naik 42,15% Jadi Rp 4,55 Juta, Ini Rinciannya
text: Bali Governor Wayan Koster set the 2027 provincial minimum wage (UMP) at Rp 4,559,287 per month, up Rp 1,351,828 or 42.15% from Rp 3,207,459 in 2026. Decree: Keputusan Gubernur Bali No. 995/03-M/HK/2026, signed Friday 20 Nov 2026, in force 1 Jan 2027. It also sets a sectoral minimum (UMSP) for star hotels of Rp 4,644,907, Rp 85,620 above the UMP. Basis: Bali Wage Council minutes No. 001/DPP-Bali/XI/2026 of 18 Nov 2026. Koster had floated Rp 4.2m (75% of the Rp 5.6m KHL, living-needs figure) as a compromise, rejected by workers' reps, who also asked for Rp 4.7m.

name: Best AI Guest Messaging for Short-Term Rentals (2026)
text: Ranking of eight AI messaging tools by Conduit, itself a ranked vendor (last updated 7 Oct 2026; low confidence on competitors). Hospitable is the only one of the five PMS vendors listed: AI Suggested Replies, Q&A Auto Replies, Message AI Assistant, Inbox AI (fully automated messaging on the Mogul plan), AI Issue Alerts, AI Copilot; free Essentials plan exists. Guesty and Hostaway appear only as PMSs that third-party AI tools (Conduit, Aeve, Enso, HostBuddy) connect to, not with native AI. Lodgify and Smoobu are not covered natively.

name: Consumo exige a dos plataformas la retirada de 8.300 anuncios de alojamientos turísticos que se ofertan como alquileres de temporada
text: Ministry press release (primary), 22 Oct 2026. Consumo asked two platforms to remove 8,318 listings advertised as seasonal rentals while allowing bookings under 31 days, the minimum under Real Decreto-ley 29/2026 (approved 6 Oct 2026). 6,772 are in Comunidad de Madrid, 6,523 in Madrid city. Viewed as misleading practice under art. 47 TRLGDCU. Notices sent via DSA notification mechanisms; platforms become directly liable and non-removal could open a sanctioning file. Cites earlier EUR 64 million sanction on Airbnb (65,000+ listings removed) and Booking removing 4,000+ listings.

name: Consumo requiere a dos grandes plataformas de alquiler turístico que retiren más de 8.000 anuncios ilícitos tras el bloqueo de casi 4.500 sólo en Madrid
text: Ministry press release (primary), Madrid 12 Nov 2026. Consumo told two large tourist-rental platforms (not named) to remove 8,352 listings advertised without a valid registration. Breakdown: 7,199 on platform one, 1,153 on platform two; no registration number 7,227 (6,263 + 964); false number 1,125 (936 + 189), being extinct room-rental numbers used for whole units. Follows the 22 Oct action in which 4,443 Madrid listings were blocked in Spain (extinct seasonal registration under Real Decreto 1312/2024, bookings of 1 to 30 nights). Those stay visible from non-Spanish IPs; Andrés Barragán wrote to the Ayuntamiento de Madrid asking it to request blocking abroad under Regulation (EU) 2022/2065. No deadline or fine amount stated.

name: Frente Amplio propone impuesto del 10% a comisiones de Airbnb y Vrbo
text: CRHoy, 16 Nov 2026: Frente Amplio, via faction head José María Villalta and its other deputies, proposes a 10% tax on commissions charged by platforms such as Airbnb and Vrbo, as a reform of the Ley Marco para la Regularización del Hospedaje No Tradicional y su Intermediación a través de Plataformas Digitales. Proceeds: 50% municipalities, 30% Banhvi, 20% ICT. All accommodation must register with the ICT before advertising, platforms must also register to operate; municipalities may limit number and concentration of rentals by district, neighbourhood or zone, and restrict them in residential buildings. Fines (base salary 462,200 colones in 2026): operators 462,200 to 9,244,000; platforms 9,244,000 to 46,220,000 (serious) and 23,110,000 to 92,440,000 (very serious). Platforms sanctionable for listing unregistered properties, omitting registration numbers in ads, ignoring takedown orders, hiding information. ICT sanctions registry/platform breaches, municipalities licences and land use. Next step: a legislative committee.

name: Consumo ordena retirar 8.352 anuncios turísticos ilegales
text: Rewrite of the ministry release, 12 Nov 2026. Ministry ordered two unnamed platforms to remove 8,352 listings: 7,199 on first, 1,153 on second; 7,227 without registration number, 1,125 with non-authentic (expired room-rental) numbers. Adds to 22 Oct action blocking 4,443 Madrid listings. Andrés Barragán sent a letter to the Ayuntamiento de Madrid with ID, URL, UTC verification date and minimum booking (1 to 30 nights) of each listing so it can get them blocked abroad.

name: Airbnb removes listings following pressure from Consumer Affairs
text: Europa Press-based report, 30 Oct 2026, on the 22 Oct action (more than 8,300 listings on two platforms, including Airbnb). Airbnb says it already took the requested measures and notified hosts, but criticised the lack of a defined framework and competence conflicts between administrations causing unnecessary confusion, calling for fair and proportionate regulation. Ministry sees misleading practice under art. 47 TRLGDCU; platforms assume direct responsibility, non-removal could lead to a sanctioning procedure. Recalls EUR 64M Airbnb sanction (65,000+ listings) and Booking removing 4,000+.

name: Kemenpar Ogah Tutup Vila Ilegal di Bali, Akan Dampingi Urus Izin
text: Deputy Tourism Minister Ni Luh Puspa said at BBTF 2026 (Nusa Dua, 30 May 2026) that the government does not intend to close unlicensed villas but will help them get licensed; OTAs must ensure all merchants have legality incl. NIB. Coaching clinics in Bali since 2025, with Pemprov Bali. Kemenpar notes rising licence applications. Deadline originally March 2026, extended to mid-year. About 1,600 businesses were threatened with removal from OTAs such as Airbnb and Tiket.com; Kemenpar is building an API-based verification system with OTA partners. Puspa: it is not only about tax, but fair competition.

name: Cerita Pemilik Kos Tak Naikkan Harga Kamar meski UMP Bali 2027 Meningkat
text: After UMP Bali 2027 rose from Rp 3,207,459 to Rp 4,559,287, workers complain of boarding-house (kos) rent rises of Rp 200-300k/month from Jan 2027 (one Padangsambian tenant: Rp 1.2m to Rp 1.5m, Threads post 22 Nov 2026, 50k views). Two Denpasar/Badung kos owners (Ni Ketut Maryati, 9 rooms at Rp 800k; Wikasari, 18 rooms) keep rent unchanged; Maryati splits electricity out via per-room meters from Jan 2027. Low direct relevance for villa operations; shows cost-of-living pressure on Bali staff.

name: UMK Badung 2027 Disepakati Rp 4,9 Juta, Sidang Berjalan Alot
text: On 23 Nov 2026 the Badung Wage Council agreed by consensus (no vote) a 2027 UMK of Rp 4.9m and a sectoral UMSK of Rp 5m, announced by Disperinaker head Anak Agung Ngurah Rai Yuda Darma. UMK rises Rp 1,108,998 or 22.63% on 2026 and is Rp 704,481 below KHL (Rp 5.6m). Union (PC FSP Par SPSI Badung, Slamet Suranto) asked Rp 5.3m then Rp 5m; Apindo held at Rp 4.8m; government offered Rp 4.9m. UMSK applies to 4- and 5-star hotels only; MSMEs about 50% of UMK. Goes to the Badung regent, then the Governor; planned in force 1 Jan 2027.

name: UMK Denpasar 2027 Direkomendasikan Naik Jadi Rp 4,78 Juta
text: Denpasar's labour office (DTKSK), head I Gusti Ayu Ngurah Raini, said the city Wage Council plenary recommended a 2027 city minimum wage (UMK) of Rp 4,787,251: 5% above the Bali UMP 2027, up 36.78% on Denpasar's 2026 UMK and 85.42% of the provincial KHL. The recommendation went to the Bali provincial government; the Governor's decision is due at the latest Wednesday 25 Nov 2026. Basis cited: UU Perlindungan Ketenagakerjaan No. 27 of 2026.

name: Verschärftes Regulativ für Kurzzeitvermietung in Wien
text: DFZ (Hannes Neumayer), 20.10.2026: Die Koalition aus SPÖ und NEOS brachte am Dienstag einen Initiativeintrag ein, der im Wohnbau-Ausschuss mit Stimmen von SPÖ, NEOS, FPÖ und Grünen eine Mehrheit fand; endgültig soll der Landtag beschließen (kein Datum genannt). Bauordnung: neuer § 7g, mindestens 80 Prozent Wohnnutzfläche, mindestens drei Zimmereinheiten, gesonderter Straßenzugang; Verfahren ab 11. Oktober nach neuem Recht. Privatausnahme 90 Tage nur für eine Wohnung mit aufrechtem Wohnsitz. Register pro Wohneinheit, Plattformen müssen stichprobenartig kontrollieren und unzulässige Inserate entfernen. Strafen bis 50.000 Euro, Register ab 1. Jänner 2027, Übergang bis Ende März 2027. Zitate: Ludwig, Hanel-Torsch, Arapović, Baupolizei-Leiter Ilja Messner.

name: Commission to investigate how Booking.com combats scams and fraud under the Digital Services Act
text: European Commission news item (dated 2026-10-21, updated 22 October 2026): the Commission opened formal proceedings to assess whether Booking.com may have breached the Digital Services Act by not diligently assessing or mitigating risks from fraudulent listings and phishing scams, and on transparency for not clearly labelling as ads listings whose providers paid for higher ranking. Three focus areas: fraudulent and non-compliant listings; phishing scams exploiting reservation and guest data; paid-for boosted listings not identifiable as ads. Primary source.

name: Airbnb guests no longer have to wash dishes or strip beds. Furious hosts are threatening to boycott and raise cleaning fees
text: Fortune (Lena Borrelli), 28 Oct 2026: Under a “reasonable house rules and requests” policy announced 20 Oct, Airbnb hosts can no longer ask guests to do tasks needing significant effort (strip bed, take trash offsite, wash dishes). It applies worldwide to reservations booked on or after 20 Nov 2026; existing bookings unaffected. Seven standard rules (max guests, quiet hours, events, pets, smoking, commercial photography, lock-up); no host fines (AirCover instead), no new rules after booking. Sanctions: warnings, listing notice, reduced search visibility. A Change.org petition has topped 10,000 signatures, up from more than 5,000 reported by CBS News days earlier; some hosts plan a booking blackout on 20 Nov and some threaten higher prices or leaving. Airbnb does not cap cleaning fees.

name: Airbnb Just Caved on Its Chores and Fees Policies—Guests Can Now Refuse These Types of Demands
text: Frommer's (Jason Cochran), 22 Oct 2026, written from the traveller's side; 'caved' refers to Airbnb siding with guests, not to a concession to hosts (it predates the 3 Nov changes). From bookings on 20 Nov 2026 hosts generally may not ask for effortful tasks (stripping bed, taking trash offsite, washing dishes), impose fines, ask guests to sign separate contracts or hand over government ID unless local law requires. Airbnb stock closed lower after the announcement. Hosts on Airbnb community pages threaten to raise cleaning fees, set earlier checkouts; a Maine host notes Airbnb promotes cleaning platform Turno at the same time. Most vitriol from absentee hosts.

name: Vrbo's 12% Commission: New Host Fees From Oct 29, 2026
text: Futurestay (author Phil Kennard): Vrbo announced on 29 Sep 2026 a flat 12% commission from 29 Oct 2026 for hosts and property managers, including PMS-connected ones. Previously most pay-per-booking hosts paid about 8% (5% plus 3% processing) and PMS-connected hosts 5%. Charged on rent plus guest fees, not taxes. Futurestay says Vrbo's help page calls it all-in but still listed a 3% processing fee, so Vrbo's share could be about $150 per $1,000 instead of $120 (this conflicts with the current help page). To keep payout, pay-per-booking hosts need about +4.5% and PMS hosts about +8%. New host terms require Vrbo rates, discounts and fees to be at least as favorable as the host's own website, and let Vrbo charge commission on direct bookings from a Vrbo inquiry within 30 days. Subscription listings switch at term end; Skift reports guest fees of 11-14% may be reduced.

name: M 3167-A Rapport de la commission de l'économie: Contrôle de la location Airbnb
text: Committee report M 3167-A, filed 17 Aug 2026 (majority report by Jacques Béné, minority by Vincent Canonica). Motion by Marc Saudan and seven co-signatories: census of short-term listings, a control body, public report within six months (2,600+ listings per Inside Airbnb). The economy committee met seven times (10 Nov 2025 to 8 Jun 2026), amended the motion (S amendment: drop the first two invites, report within twelve months, adopted 7-6-1) but then rejected the amended motion 9 to 5 (PLR, MCG, UDC, LC against; S, Ve, LJS for), the majority holding that Conseil d'Etat measures (registration, notification duty, automated monitoring of the 90-day cap) already answer the concerns. The plenary later reversed this and approved the amended motion on 5 Nov 2026 (per press). The report carries no plenary vote date. The suggested voted-text URL MV02347 is Motion 2347 of 8 Oct 2021, a different motion.

name: Guesty acquires Smily, deepening its investment in France's booming short-term rental market
text: Guesty press release, 17 Sep 2026 (New York & Paris): Guesty has completed the acquisition of Smily (formerly BookingSync), a leading PMS and channel manager in France founded 2005 by Sébastien Grosjean, open to paying customers since 2010. Terms not disclosed; all five Smily founders and some shareholders reinvest part of the proceeds in Guesty equity. Smily processed more than €3.3bn in bookings for 13 million travelers and is a Booking.com Premier Plus Connectivity Partner for 2026. Guesty says it runs 500,000+ properties in 100+ countries, has $410m funding (KKR, Apax Digital, etc.) and shipped 300+ features in 2026.

name: Vrbo Service Fee: Commission Structure Change
text: Hospitable support article (updated Nov 2026): Vrbo's 12% commission began rolling out 29 Oct 2026, staggered per account. It applies to Pay-Per-Booking hosts now and Pay-Per-Subscription hosts when their annual term ends, whether or not they use a PMS; it includes Vrbo's payment processing and Vrbo does not discount it for third-party processors. Hospitable as merchant of record adds 3.9% (2.7% AU). Commission is on nightly rate plus host fees (cleaning, pet, boat); taxes and refundable deposits are separate. Vrbo bills fees to the card on file. Hospitable automatically raised Vrbo markups on 29 Oct (opt-out closed 28 Oct 23:59 PT) so payout stays flat, e.g. 10% markup at 8% commission becomes 15% at 12%; Vrbo Partner connection hosts can include fees. Vrbo Legacy listings are re-priced by Vrbo (first 12 months of dates first).

name: Vrbo's New 12% Commission: What It Means & How to Prepare
text: Hostaway says Vrbo moves pay-per-booking hosts to a standard 12% commission from Thursday 29 Oct 2026, applied to bookings made from that date (not stay date). Previously PMS-connected hosts paid 5%; hosts without PMS paid 5% plus 3% processing; annual subscribers move at subscription expiry as Vrbo retires the Pay-Per-Subscription program. The 12% covers rental amount plus guest fees such as cleaning and pet fees, and includes payment processing; Australia, Europe and New Zealand may be higher. To keep a 5% net payout prices must rise about 7.95% (950/0.88), not 7%. Hostaway offers a Vrbo-specific whole-number markup (Listings > Price & Fees) and a Vrbo Host Channel Fee setting of 12% for reporting; it recommends changes by 28 Oct.

name: Booking, Over 18 Thousand Hotels in Class Action Demand Billions in Compensation
text: Adnkronos report: SHCA filed the third and final group of participants in the class action against Booking Holdings at the Amsterdam District Court; 18,135 hotels, +68% in three months; 10,783 in July vs 3,087 at the January 2026 start. Compensation for anti-competitive rate parity clauses 2004-2024; SHCA estimates claim could reach several billion euros plus interest. First hearing scheduled for 2027. Initiative head Volker Soyez and HOTREC president Alexandros Vassilikos quoted.

name: Airbnb bets big on multibillion-dollar hotel opportunity
text: Hotel Dive (Jenna Graber, 16 Nov 2026): Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said on the Q3 call (early Nov) hotels are one of the biggest opportunities ahead and that Airbnb will do multiple billions of dollars in hotel revenue in coming years; hotels are still a single-digit share of nights but grow markedly faster than the core. Q2 hotel nights grew about three times faster than homes. Airbnb lists thousands of boutique and independent hotels in 60+ top destinations; in Q3 it signed Lark Hotels (75+ properties). About 35% of guests whose first booking is a hotel book a home within a year. VP hotels Andrea D'Amico (joined June, 18+ years at Booking.com) says franchised and branded hotels are likely next; Pepijn Rijvers (ex Tripadvisor and Booking.com) joined as chief business officer in September. HotelTonight was bought in 2019.

name: HotellerieSuisse fordert klare Regeln für Kurzzeitvermietung
text: HotellerieSuisse, 16.09.2026: Neues Positionspapier. Rund 70 Prozent der Schweizer Kurzzeitvermietungsangebote sind professionell oder semi-professionell (2019: rund 20 Prozent). Forderung: schweizweite Registrierungspflicht, Datenaustausch Plattformen-Behörden-Statistik, nationale Mindeststandards bei kantonaler und kommunaler Steuerung; keine pauschalen Verbote oder starren Limiten. Motion 24.4165 de Quattro im Nationalrat im Sommer 2026 angenommen; HotellerieSuisse will, dass der Ständerat folgt. Direktor Christian Hürlimann.

name: Over 10,000 European hotels now part of landmark collective action against Booking.com
text: HOTREC release (organiser-side): SHCA, a Dutch not-for-profit foundation, added 7,696 hotels to its collective action against Booking.com before the Amsterdam District Court, now 10,783 hotels, up from 3,087 at launch on 30 January 2026. Damages sought for price parity clauses 2004-2024. A third and final expansion is planned for autumn 2026 (about 18,000 expected); free registration at mybookingclaim.com until 11 Sept 2026. Supported by HOTREC and more than 30 national associations. Dutch courts have jurisdiction under Booking.com's terms; the Amsterdam court knows the matter from related proceedings since 2020. HOTREC's Jan 30 release (read, not stored) ties the claim to the CJEU judgment of 19 Sept 2024.

name: Basel will Registrierungspflicht für Airbnb-Vermietungen
text: htr.ch (keystone-sda), 23.09.2026: Der Grosse Rat Basel-Stadt überwies am Mittwoch (23.9.) eine Motion von SP-Grossrat Ivo Balmer mit 68 zu 24 Stimmen bei einer Enthaltung 'erstmals' an die Regierung. Anbieter sollen sich vor Beginn der Vermietung bei der zuständigen Behörde registrieren; Ziel: Wohnraumschutz, Kontrolle des Wohnanteils durch das Bau- und Gastgewerbeinspektorat. Dafür SP, Grüne, Basta, GLP, Mitte/EVP; dagegen FDP und Mehrheit von SVP und LDP. Balmer hatte schon 2024 einen Vorstoss (u.a. 90-Tage-Limite zur Prüfung) eingereicht. Heute: Gasttaxe, Betriebsbewilligung ab sechs Betten. Es ist nur die Überweisung, kein Gesetz.

name: Klare Regeln für Kurzzeitvermietungen
text: htr.ch, 17.09.2026: Interview mit Magdalena Glausen (Leiterin Politik HotellerieSuisse). Der Verband fordert eine nationale Registrierungspflicht, standardisierten Datenaustausch, eine schweizweite Definition, ab wann Vermietung gewerblich ist; lehnt pauschale Verbote und 90-Tage-Regel ab; Steuerung bei Kantonen und Gemeinden. Motion 24.4165 von Jacqueline de Quattro wurde im Nationalrat in der Sommersession 2026 angenommen und der Kommission zugewiesen. L-GAV-Kontrolle: jährlich rund 30 Betriebe gewerblich ohne Regulierung.

name: Airbnb Floats Price-Matching: How AI Agents and Direct Bookings Are Reshaping Travel Value
text: The Hype Magazine (Dr Jerry Doby), 21 Nov 2026. Affiliate-linked rewrite of the Skift article ('Originally referenced from skift.com'), same headline stem. Repeats Chesky's quote and Skift's 16-listing Instinct test (direct cheaper in 10, 1% to 42%). Adds details not visible in Skift's truncated text and unverified here: Uniko Living in Mexico City $145 on Airbnb vs $84 direct; hotels mostly won direct while apartments split 3-3 with one tie; a '45 listings scanned, 23 without direct portal' figure that conflicts with the 16-listing framing; Savvy CEO Eric Goldreyer on price-match options; Vrbo parity clauses. Not independent.

name: 5 Ribu Vila di Bali Ajukan Izin usai Penertiban Online Travel Agent
text: Bali Governor Wayan Koster said on 21 Sep 2026 (DPRD Bali) that the crackdown on unlicensed villas sold by online travel agents is working: about 5,000 villa businesses applied for licences (2025-2026). It targets villas in Badung, Denpasar, Gianyar and Tabanan. Koster called in eight large OTAs (e.g. Airbnb, Agoda, Booking.com; HQ Singapore), threatened sanctions if they keep marketing unlicensed lodging, and says they agreed to list only licensed lodging and push owners to get permits. Licensed hotels are 80-90% occupied daily and hotel-restaurant tax revenue is up more than Rp300 billion year on year (same period 2025 vs 2026). Oversight is run with the Tourism Ministry and regencies/cities, who survey unlicensed accommodation inventory.

name: El Gobierno pide la retirada de más de 8.300 anuncios ilícitos de pisos turísticos
text: EFE wire via Infobae, 12 Nov 2026. Consumo (minister Pablo Bustinduy) demanded removal of 8,352 listings advertised without licence or with a false registration number on two large platforms: 7,227 lack identification, 1,125 use an extinct number of room rentals though offering whole homes. Follows 22 Oct action on 4,443 Madrid listings blocked in Spain; ministry warned the Ayuntamiento de Madrid the platform keeps them visible from non-Spanish IPs and urged it to request blocking abroad. Platforms unnamed.

name: Terancam Dihapus dari Platform Online, Ribuan Vila Ilegal di Bali Diminta Urus Izin
text: Tourism Ministry (Kemenpar) will remove about 1,600 unlicensed lodgings still listed on Agoda, Booking.com, Airbnb and Tiket.com from 1 Aug 2026 (announced by Minister Widianti Putri Wardhana at a Jakarta press conference on 26 May 2026). Deputy Minister Ni Luh Puspa said at Bali & Beyond Travel Fair, Nusa Dua, on 30 May 2026 that the ministry does not delete them but asks OTAs to require all merchants to have legality including an NIB; programme running since 2025 with coaching clinics, in collaboration with Pemprov Bali. Original target was March 2026, extended to mid-2026.

name: Wien dreht Airbnb den Hahn zu – das ändert sich ab 2027
text: KOSMO, 22.10.2026: behauptet, der Wiener Landtag habe am 20. Oktober 2026 die strengeren Regeln beschlossen (Bauordnung plus Kurzzeitvermietungsregister), mit Stimmen von SPÖ, NEOS, FPÖ und Grünen; ÖVP kritisiert fehlendes Begutachtungsverfahren. Das widerspricht DFZ, wonach am 20.10. nur der Wohnbau-Ausschuss entschied. Register startet 1. Jänner 2027, Übergang für bereits inserierte Wohnungen bis Ende März 2027, Plattformen müssen kontrollieren und Inserate entfernen, bis 50.000 Euro Strafe als Höchstbetrag, 90-Tage-Ausnahme nur eine Wohnung.

name: Genève renonce à une nouvelle entité pour contrôler Airbnb
text: La Télé / Keystone-ATS, published 5 Nov 2026 (a Thursday): the Grand Conseil genevois modified 'jeudi' (i.e. 5 Nov 2026) Marc Saudan's motion, rejecting a new control body in favour of a new IT tool, and accepted it as amended by 65 votes to 31 with one abstention. Original invites: census of all short-term listings, ad hoc supervisory authority, public report in six months; the amendment kept only an evaluation report within twelve months. Council of State plans regulatory changes (foreign-guest notification for all hosts, official number displayed by platforms, signal to the cantonal housing office and trade police at 90 nights); a credit was voted (Nicolas Walder, DT). Over 2,600 listings cited; 90-day cap upheld by the Federal Court.

name: Geneva tightens checks on Airbnb rentals without creating a new supervisory body
text: Le Temps with ATS, 6 Nov 2026: on Thursday (5 Nov 2026 by the calendar; the article is dated Friday 6 Nov) the Geneva Grand Council amended and then approved, by 65 votes to 31 with one abstention, a motion by Marc Saudan (independent, formerly LJS) that originally asked for a census of all short-term listings, a dedicated supervisory authority and a public report within six months. An amendment dropped the authority and the census and kept only an evaluation report within twelve months. The Council of State will act by regulation: foreign-guest registration extended to all hosts (today only hotels), an official number per rental that platforms must display, and an alert to the cantonal housing office and trade police once the 90-night limit is reached; funding is approved (Nicolas Walder). Over 2,600 listings are cited.

name: Top 5 Guesty Competitors & Alternatives to Try in 2026
text: Lodgify's own comparison page (last updated October 2026; competitor claims low confidence). Lodgify has a unified inbox with built-in AI writing assistant to draft guest replies, and Lodgify AI Co-Host in early access (prepares actions for approval). Guesty's small-host product Guesty for Hosts was sunset in 2026 and folded into Guesty Lite (1-3 listings). Hostaway markets AI-generated guest replies; Hospitable: AI Guest Issue Alerts from Host plan, Mogul adds fully automated messaging via InboxAI. Smoobu: paid-only from 2026, plans Professional Flex ~EUR 29, Pre-Paid ~EUR 35, Teams Pro+ ~EUR 55; no AI mentioned.

name: Penertiban Akomodasi Ilegal Bali: Gubernur Koster Kumpulkan OTA untuk Tata Ulang Pariwisata
text: Merdeka (citing AntaraNews, dated 2026-01-04 by the fetcher) reports Governor Koster will gather OTAs in 2026 to filter illegal accommodation such as villas and hotels not paying tax in Denpasar, jointly with the Tourism Ministry, which has already sent a letter convening OTA players. Koster says the process will be gradual. Hotel-restaurant tax (PHR) rose in all regencies in 2025; official hotel occupancy 70-85%, 7.1 million foreign and 9.28 million domestic tourists in 2025 (Koster, no PAD figures given).

name: El ultimátum del Ministerio de Consumo a los alquileres turísticos: 8.300 anuncios ilegales que deben desaparecer
text: Explainer, 16 Nov 2026 (Diego Servente), based on the ministry release. 8,352 listings on two unnamed platforms (7,199 and 1,153); per-platform split 6,263/964 no number, 936/189 false. 4,443 Madrid listings blocked in Spain but visible abroad; letter by Andrés Barragán cites Regulation (EU) 2022/2065. Mentions RD 1312/2024 extinct seasonal registry and RDL 29/2026 (6 Oct, stays 31 days to 12 months). Adds, without attribution to the release, that illicit advertising may be a grave infraction with fines up to EUR 100,000, exceedable by four to six times the illicit benefit. No deadline stated.

name: Airbnb Expands Hotel Push With Price Match, Bigger Rebates
text: NerdWallet (Benjamin Din), 20 May 2026, from Airbnb's 2026 Summer Release event in San Francisco. Airbnb adds independent and boutique (non-chain) hotels in select cities such as London, New York, Madrid, Paris, Rome and Singapore. Listings with a 'featured hotel' badge give up to 15% back in Airbnb credit (up from up to 10%), credited within 24 hours of checkout and usable within one year. Select hotel listings carry a price-match guarantee: if the same stay is cheaper elsewhere, the difference is paid as Airbnb credit, up to $400, usable within a year. Conditions: booking must show eligibility at checkout; the lower rate needs the same dates, room type, guest count and a cancellation policy no stricter than Airbnb's.

name: Ab 2027 Registrierungspflicht bei Kurzzeitvermietung in Wien
text: news.at (APA), 19.09.2026: Wien kündigt neue Verschärfung an: Registrierungspflicht auf Basis des WKVRG, 'noch im November' im Landtag zu beschliessen (tatsächlich am 20.10. beschlossen), Inkrafttreten 1.1.2027, Übergangsfrist für bestehende Angebote bis Ende Q1 2027. Strafen bis 50.000 Euro. Bauordnung: mindestens 80 Prozent der Nutzfläche der Regelgeschosse für Wohnzwecke, Anträge seit Sommer werden nach neuem Recht geprüft. 305 Umwandlungsanträge 2025; rund 550 Strafanträge und fast 2.500 Anzeigen bis Juli 2026. Mietervereinigung begrüsst, FPÖ und Grüne kritisieren. Inhaltsgleich mit der Stadt-Wien-Meldung vom 19.09.

name: More than 1,325 Dutch hotels join mass claim lawsuit against Booking.com
text: ANP via NL Times: KHN reports 1,326 Dutch hotels (headline says 1,325) in the collective lawsuit; EU-wide total above 18,000; hearing in Amsterdam expected 2027. Hotels seek a share of commissions collected 2004-2024; CJEU ruled in 2024 the clauses breached competition law. Booking.com calls the claims unfounded and will contest; cites an Amsterdam ruling in a similar case that hotels failed to show restriction or damage. Separate Dutch consumer class action (Consumentenbond and CCC) filed Nov 2025. Earlier this year Amsterdam court ruled in a related case that claims were not time-barred; a German court ordered Booking.com to pay damages.

name: Wien verschärft Regeln für Airbnb
text: ORF Wien, 19.09.2026: Bürgermeister Ludwig (SPÖ) kündigte im Sommergespräch strengere Regeln an. Das WKVRG soll noch im November im Landtag beschlossen werden, Inkrafttreten 1. Jänner 2027, Übergangsfrist für bestehende Angebote bis Ende des ersten Quartals 2027, Strafen bis 50.000 Euro. Umwidmungen werden eingeschränkt (80 Prozent Wohnnutzung). Reaktionen: Mietervereinigung (Georg Niedermühlbichler) begrüßt, Verband der Apartmentvermieter (VDAV) grundsätzlich positiv aber Kritik an Umsetzung, FPÖ (Dominik Nepp) spricht von Nebelkerze, Grüne (Judith Pühringer) fordern mehr.

name: Kurzzeitvermietung: Beschluss am Dienstag
text: ORF Wien, 16.10.2026: Bürgermeister Ludwig kündigt an, dass der Landtag am Dienstag (20.10.) weitere Verschärfungen bei Kurzzeitvermietung beschließen soll: Register mit Pflichtnummer ab Jahresbeginn 2027, drei Monate Übergangsfrist, Plattformen wie Airbnb und Booking.com müssen Angaben prüfen und ungültige Inserate entfernen. Umwidmung erschwert (80 Prozent Wohnnutzung), rückwirkend für Ansuchen seit 10. Oktober. Bestehende 90-Tage-Regel seit 2024 bleibt.

name: Landtag beschloss neue AirBnB-Regeln
text: ORF Wien, 20.10.2026: Der Wiener Landtag hat die neuen Regeln für Kurzzeitvermietung beschlossen. Ab 1. Jänner 2027 müssen sich alle Kurzzeitvermieter registrieren; ohne Nummer kein Inserat; Plattformen dürfen nur registrierte Angebote zulassen. Drei Monate Übergangsfrist, ab April droht ohne Registrierung das Aus. Parallel verschärfte Umwidmungsregeln: mindestens 80 Prozent eines Gebäudes bleiben Wohnzwecken vorbehalten. Bürgermeister Michael Ludwig (SPÖ) spricht von Schlupflöchern; der Verband der Apartmentvermieter widerspricht.

name: Booking.com: Δύο κρίσιμα μέτωπα το 2027 για 18.135 Ευρωπαίους και Έλληνες ξενοδόχους
text: Alexandros Vassilikos (HOTREC and Hellenic Chamber of Hotels) calls the Greek Competition Commission rapporteur's opinion 'extremely inadequate': no fine, but acceptance of Booking.com's commitments; plenary on 19 Jan 2027 (moved from 28 Dec 2026). Preliminary view: serious concerns of abuse of dominance in Greek online hotel booking, focusing on the ranking mechanism and preferred-hotel programmes that may create incentives to offer better prices/terms on Booking.com than on rival platforms. Commitments were in public consultation until July 2026. Pan-European collective action: 18,135 hotels, almost 1,000 Greek, filed at Amsterdam District Court by Stichting Hotel Claims Alliance (SHCA) with HOTREC and over 30 national associations; parity clauses 2004-2024. HOTREC announced on 30 Oct 2026 growth of 68% in three months from 10,783 (July) to 18,135 (October), start January with 3,087. First hearing expected in 2027. Booking.com disputes the claims; Sept 2026 changes to programme transparency and ranking were announced.

name: Bürgermeister Ludwig: Wien ist Vorbild beim Schutz von leistbaren Wohnungen für die Bevölkerung
text: OTS-Presseaussendung des Büros Bürgermeister Ludwig vom 19.09.2026, inhaltsgleich mit der Stadt-Wien-Seite: WKVRG soll noch im November im Wiener Landtag beschlossen werden, Inkrafttreten 1. Jänner 2027, Übergangsfrist für bereits angebotene Wohnungen bis Ablauf des 1. Quartals 2027. Registrierungsnummer in Inseraten Pflicht, Strafen bis 50.000 Euro pro Verstoß, Mindeststrafen 2.000 Euro bei Wiederholung, Umwidmung nur bei mindestens 80 Prozent Wohnnutzfläche. Kontakt: Mario Dujakovic, Mediensprecher.

name: Airbnb targets first-half 2027 for AI agent launch
text: PhocusWire (Cathy Walsh), 6 Nov 2026: On the Q3 call (Thu 5 Nov) CEO Brian Chesky said Airbnb will begin rolling out its AI travel agent in the first half of 2027, with a generative UI of hundreds of travel components; sponsored listings follow the agent launch. Q3 revenue rose 19% to $4.9 billion (16% ex-FX), ADR up 4%, GBV up 21% to $27.7 billion, nights and seats booked up 16% to 155 million (reserve now, pay later added about 3 points). Net income $1.9 billion, adjusted EBITDA up 22% to $2.5 billion. App nights up 29% (66% of nights). Amex partnership: thousands of bookings, nearly a quarter from new travelers. Airbnb handles nearly half a million bookings a day.

name: European Commission investigating Booking.com's handling of scams, fraud
text: PhocusWire (Abby Crotty): the Commission launched a DSA investigation into Booking.com after a preliminary probe covering risk assessment reports from 2023 to 2026 and information requests in September 2025 and May 2026. Booking.com has been a VLOP since April 2023; fines up to 6% of global annual turnover are possible. The opening of formal proceedings allows interim measures and a non-compliance finding; Booking.com can settle with commitments. Booking.com says it is cooperating fully. Commission EVP Henna Virkkunen is quoted. Booking.com confirmed a data breach in April 2026 and was designated a DMA gatekeeper in May 2024.

name: Booking Holdings stellt die Booking Partner Division vor, um Innovationen im B2B-Reisesektor voranzutreiben
text: Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG) announced on 18 Nov 2026 (New York, PR Newswire, German version) the Booking Partner Division, a new global B2B organisation built on Booking.com Strategic Partnerships and Rocket Travel by Agoda. It becomes operational in January 2027 under a shared leadership structure and serves banks, financial institutions, airlines, online travel agencies, travel-tech platforms, affiliates, advertisers and publishers. Offer: white-label, API, branded and chain B2B rate distribution solutions over a portfolio of more than 4.7 million properties, over 33 million accommodation listings, 500+ airlines and 200+ car rental companies. Omri Morgenshtern is quoted as head of the division, Glenn Fogel as CEO of Booking Holdings; AI features for partners are promised without dates or financial targets.

name: PetScreening and HostBuddy AI Launch Integration to Streamline Pet Policy Management & Service Animal Verification for Vacation Rental Hosts
text: PR Newswire press release, 12 Nov 2026 (Mooresville, N.C.). PetScreening announced an integration with HostBuddy AI, the independent AI guest-messaging platform: guests are automatically guided through PetScreening's pet and assistance animal screening from within HostBuddy's messaging; updates arrive via Action Items, Slack, email, SMS and WhatsApp. Claims pet-friendly listings earn 24% higher revenue per booking and three times as many bookings (no source given). Quotes from John Bradford (founder and CEO, PetScreening) and Jay Ullrich (CEO, HostBuddy AI).

name: PetScreening and HostBuddy AI Launch Integration to Streamline Pet Policy Management & Service Animal Verification for Vacation Rental Hosts
text: PR Newswire press release, 12 Nov 2026 (Mooresville, N.C.): PetScreening announced an integration with HostBuddy AI, an AI guest messaging platform for STR operators. Guests are guided automatically through PetScreening's pet and assistance-animal screening; updates arrive via Action Items, Slack, email, SMS and WhatsApp. PetScreening claims pet-friendly listings generate 24% higher revenue per booking and three times as many bookings. Quoted: John Bradford (founder and CEO, PetScreening), Jay Ullrich (CEO, HostBuddy AI). Vendor press release, claims unverified. HostBuddy AI is a third-party company.

name: Booking.com: Legal battle with 18,135 European hoteliers set for 2027
text: First hearing in the collective lawsuit of more than 18,100 European hoteliers against Booking.com expected in 2027 at the Amsterdam District Court; claim covers price parity clauses 2004-2024. Participants grew from about 3,000 to 18,135 hotels (figure presented by the Hellenic Chamber of Hotels, HCH, at its general assembly at XENIA), including hundreds of Greek hotels. In parallel, the Hellenic Competition Commission examines a complaint by HCH of May 2022 against Booking.com B.V. (abuse of dominance); the plenary hearing moved from 28 Dec 2026 to 19 Jan 2027, focused on the platform's conduct and proposed commitments. HCH president and HOTREC president Alexandros Vassilikos says the dispute is about hotels' autonomy and competition, not only commissions.

name: The AI Guest Whisperer Taking Over Vacation Rentals
text: PYMNTS, 27 Apr 2026: Hostaway says more than 70% of vacation rental managers now use AI tools, nearly double six months earlier. Pricing (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse) is the most common entry point. bnbme Holiday Homes CEO Vinayak Mahtani told Forbes the in-house AI assistant handles about 70% of guest needs alone, escalating to humans below 90% confidence. Forge Holiday Group (CEO Graham Donoghue) spends $30,000-50,000 a month with Anthropic on tokens; its Vivid Stay tool turns photos into video in 25 minutes versus $2,000-3,000 per property before. Casago CEO Steve Schwab says token costs are 20-30% of compute cost. Holmes Beach, Florida saw higher STR compliance after an AI monitoring platform (per WFLA). Donoghue and Schwab expect AI to disintermediate some OTAs.

name: Booking Holdings is combining Booking.com and Agoda B2B units
text: Quartz (Ella Rodrigo, 18 Nov 2026): Booking Holdings announced the Booking Partner Division, merging the partner operations of Booking.com and Agoda, operational from January 2027, built on Booking.com Strategic Partnerships and Rocket Travel by Agoda. Solutions: White Label, API, Branded Solutions, Chain B2B Rates Distribution; 4.7m+ properties, 33m+ listings, 500+ airlines, 200+ car rental providers. Omri Morgenshtern, also CEO of Agoda (per CNBC), leads it; Glenn Fogel is CEO of Booking Holdings. Morgenshtern declined to quantify revenue or profit contribution and put the total addressable market at $2tn (per CNBC); a vertical AI agent for partners is planned.

name: Booking Holdings is combining Booking.com and Agoda B2B units
text: Quartz (Ella Rodrigo), 18 Nov 2026: Booking Holdings announced the Booking Partner Division, merging partner operations of Booking.com and Agoda, operational from January 2027, led by Omri Morgenshtern (also Agoda CEO, per CNBC). Solutions: White Label, API, Branded Solutions, Chain B2B Rates Distribution; 4.7 million+ properties, 33 million+ listings, 500+ airlines, 200+ car rental providers. Morgenshtern (via CNBC) gave no revenue/profit figure, put TAM at $2 trillion and is 'super optimistic' about a vertical AI agent for partners. Glenn Fogel is CEO of Booking Holdings.

name: Guesty For Hosts has shut down: how to choose a replacement (and the part most guides miss)
text: Recal (an ops-tool vendor, low confidence on competitors). Guesty For Hosts shut down on 31 May 2026; technical support ended 15 January. Automated messages, templates and pricing rules did not transfer, not even to Guesty Lite and Pro. Recommends Smoobu (basic scheduled messaging), Hospitable (strongest, full automation plus AI reply drafts), Lodgify (AI reply drafts, no full automation), Hostaway (full, advanced messaging, quote-based pricing).

name: Vrbo New Features 2026: Property Manager Guide | RedAwning
text: RedAwning blog (Sara Levy-Lambert, 8 Sep 2026; a vendor selling channel management, secondary reporting citing Skift, PhocusWire, Rental Scale-Up). On 1 Sep 2026 Expedia Group shipped 12 Vrbo products, six live and six coming soon. Sponsored listings: auction, top two positions, pay per booked night, no rate card published; pilot with nine partners (AvantStay among them) averaged 40% booking growth and 39% revenue gain. New cancellation tiers (full refund to 5 or 1 day before check-in) and non-refundable rates require channel managers to push multiple rate plans. More than 40% of Vrbo Q2 2026 bookings came from host-funded promotions (about 33% in Q1). Premier Host thresholds: 0% partner-initiated cancellations, 99% acceptance, 4.6 review score. Vrbo Payments pilot inside Escapia. No mention of the 12% fee or payment processing fees.

name: Airbnb Floats Price-Matching: A Skift Test Shows Where Direct Booking Wins
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 20 Nov 2026. Using the AI agent Instinct, Skift compared 16 Airbnb listings with the properties' own website rates: direct was cheaper in 10, by as much as 42%, and one was essentially a tie. When an X account asked whether Airbnb profits would suffer if AI agents compared prices before booking, CEO Brian Chesky replied 'You presume we could never offer a price-match guarantee.' Skift stresses this was not an announcement for short-term rentals (Airbnb recently started price-matching for hotels) but a signal Airbnb could, and may eventually have to. Fetched text is truncated at about 1,000 characters (paywall); the rest of the article was not available.

name: Airbnb’s New Policy for Hosts: Don’t Ask Guests to Wash Dishes or Strip Beds
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 21 Oct 2026: In a Tuesday (20 Oct) email titled “Important Changes to House Rules”, Airbnb told hosts that starting November 20 they can choose from seven standard house rules and are “generally not allowed” to ask guests to wash dishes, strip beds or take out the garbage. It is the first published Airbnb house rules policy spelling out reasonable host requests. Repeat violators could get a notice on the listing, lower search visibility or other actions under the terms of service (cancelled bookings, loss of Superhost or Guest Favorite status, account suspension). A new terms provision bars hosts from requiring separate rental agreements, with exceptions (monthly stays, Airbnb Luxe, optional amenities). Article text is truncated at the source.

name: Airbnb Pitches Hotels: We Care More About Stays Than Booking.com Does
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 18 Nov 2026. Airbnb is courting independent hotels with a pitch aimed at Booking.com: unlike Booking, it says, it is built around stays. Lou Zameryka, Airbnb's global head of hotel enterprise and connectivity partnerships, told Skift on Wednesday (18 Nov) after speaking at the Phocuswright conference in Hollywood, Florida, that Booking is 'not hotel-centric'. Fetched text is truncated at about 490 characters (paywall); no commission figures or further executives are available.

name: Airbnb Pitches Hotels: We Care More About Stays Than Booking.com Does
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 18 Nov 2026. Airbnb is courting independent hotels with a pitch aimed at Booking.com: it says it is built around stays. Lou Zameryka, Airbnb's global head of hotel enterprise and connectivity partnerships, told Skift on Wednesday (18 Nov) after speaking at the Phocuswright conference in Hollywood, Florida, that Booking is not hotel-centric. Only the first ~450 characters were retrievable (paywall); commission rates, hotel counts and further quotes are NOT in the fetched text.

name: Airbnb Updates House Rules After Host Pushback
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 16 Nov 2026 (listed as “Airbnb Makes Concessions on House Rules After Host Pushback”): Airbnb partially walked back the October policy after public host objections, but the core restrictions still take effect 20 Nov 2026. Under the 3 Nov update “Requests” become “additional rules” that guests “are expected to comply with”, covering dishes in the sink, used towels, recycling. Hosts may require a separate rental agreement when an insurer demands one. Still barred: checkout chores, host-imposed fines, rules added after booking, collecting guest IDs, emails, phone numbers or signed agreements absent a legal, building or insurer requirement. Review timeline: listing reviews run 20 Nov 2026 to March 2027, at least 20 days to fix, one appeal per flagged rule. Hosts can cancel without penalty only if a guest breaks one of the seven standard rules.

name: Airbnb's Pivot: Inside Its New Push Into Hotels
text: Skift (Sean O'Neill), 21 Sep 2026. CEO Brian Chesky, at a Goldman Sachs conference in September, said he stopped being ideological about hotels and wants them to become one of Airbnb's next multi-billion-dollar businesses. Airbnb is curating supply and taking a lower cut than Booking.com or Expedia, betting on its audience (over 1.6 billion devices a year). Per AirDNA, 3,939 hotels used a new listing format across hundreds of markets as of 4 Sep 2026. Hotels were still a single-digit percentage of nights booked in Q2 (Chesky). Text truncated at ~970 characters (paywall).

name: Booking Holdings Leaves Priceline Out of B2B Unit Amid FTC Scrutiny
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 18 Nov 2026: Booking Holdings carved Priceline out of the new Booking Partner Division because of a potential FTC complaint against the brand; Omri Morgenshtern (division head, Agoda CEO) told Skift at Phocuswright that it created 'operational complexities' and Priceline 'will keep serving their partners'. The original plan was to merge Rocket Travel by Agoda, Booking.com partnerships and the Priceline Partner Network; now the first two unify and the Priceline Partner Network stays separate. Booking took a $1 billion Q3 charge tied to the FTC matter (alleged unfair or deceptive practices on disclosures, fees, customer support, billing). Morgenshtern runs the division from New York while staying Agoda CEO, supported by recently promoted COO Ittai Chorev; Booking likely to break out B2B financials like Expedia.

name: The Pressures on Expedia B2B
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal, 23 Nov 2026): Expedia Group's B2B segment, the engine of most recent growth, is set to slow. In Q3 B2B gross bookings grew 19% year over year and B2B revenue 23%. At the 4 Nov results, CFO Derek Andersen said Q4 B2B growth would moderate against a tough comparison (Q4 2025 gross bookings +24% to $8.7bn, helped by heavy marketing from large partners), citing also soft demand around the US election cycle, geopolitical disruption hitting long-haul travel, and a fall sale that pulled bookings into Q3. Bernstein senior analyst Richard Clarke called B2B the weak spot of an otherwise strong quarter. Cached text is truncated (983 chars, paywall): nothing visible on Vrbo, API partners, Booking Partner Division or AI agents.

name: The AI Agent Is Travel's Ad Blocker
text: Skift (Rafat Ali column), 18 Nov 2026. AI agents booking for travellers do not buy on impulse, threatening upsell profits (MCR Hotels CEO Tyler Morse at Skift Commerce Summit, November). Citizens analysts, in a 15 Nov report testing AI booking agents Instinct and Meta's Muse, found them underwhelming but ranked Expedia most exposed, then Booking Holdings, with Airbnb most insulated. Morgan Stanley's October analysis looked at similar questions. Text truncated (paywall).

name: Vrbo to Double Commissions as It Plays Catch-Up to Airbnb
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal, 29 Sep 2026): Vrbo, Expedia Group's vacation rental brand, said on Tuesday it is moving hosts and property managers to a flat 12% fee from 29 October (2026). PMS-connected property managers currently pay 5%, hosts without PMS pay an 8% commission. According to AirDNA about 55% of listings globally connect to Vrbo via PMS, 51% in the US. Guest fees currently 11-14%; a vacation rental expert says Vrbo plans to cut them drastically, though Vrbo's FAQ says travelers will still see a service fee in most cases. Skift's framing: Vrbo catching up to Airbnb. Text accessible only in part (840 chars).

name: Vrbo to Double Commissions as It Plays Catch-Up to Airbnb
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal, 29 Sep 2026; only the first 840 characters were retrievable, text cut off mid-sentence). Vrbo, the Expedia Group vacation rental brand, said Tuesday it is moving hosts and property managers to a flat 12% fee from 29 Oct 2026. PMS-connected property managers paid 5%, hosts not connected to a PMS paid 8%. About 55% of listings globally connect to Vrbo via PMS (51% in the US), per AirDNA. The host note did not address guest fees (currently 11-14%); an unnamed expert said Vrbo plans to cut them drastically, and Vrbo's FAQ says some guest fees would remain.

name: Top AI Tools for Vacation Rental Automation in 2026: The Ultimate Guide
text: Smoobu's own blog (vendor self-description). Smoobu's AI translates message templates into 10 languages; every translation is marked 'Translated with AI' for review. AI translation of guest messages and replies in the inbox is rolling out one account at a time. Smoobu has no ChatGPT or Gemini built in; hosts should draft with external AI and paste in. Lists third-party tools (Breezeway Assist, HostBuddy AI, Conduit, PriceLabs, Enso Connect) for AI messaging. Page date 2026-02-11 per metadata; text does not date the rollout. No AI reply drafting or auto-reply is claimed for Smoobu.

name: Spain orders removal of 8,352 illegal tourist rental adverts
text: English-language rewrite, 18 Nov 2026. Ministry of Consumer Affairs ordered two unidentified platforms to remove 8,352 listings: 7,199 on one, 1,153 on another; 7,227 no registration number, 1,125 invalid. text: Stadt Wien (Primärquelle): Bürgermeister Michael Ludwig kündigt ein neues Wiener Kurzzeitvermietungsregistergesetz (WKVRG) an, das noch im November 2026 im Wiener Landtag beschlossen werden soll und am 1. Jänner 2027 in Kraft tritt. Bestehende Gastgeber haben eine Übergangsfrist bis Ablauf des 1. Quartals 2027, neue Gastgeber unterliegen ab 1. Jänner 2027 der Pflicht. Registrierungsnummer muss in Inseraten angegeben werden, Plattformen dürfen nur registrierte Wohnungen anbieten. Strafen bis 50.000 Euro pro Verstoß, bei Wiederholung Mindeststrafen von 2.000 Euro. Umwidmung in Beherbergungsstätten: mindestens 80 Prozent der Nutzflächen der Regelgeschoße müssen Wohnzwecken dienen, gilt für Verfahren seit Sommer 2026. 2025: 305 Anträge zu Beherbergungsstätten, 132 bewilligt; 2.484 Anzeigen seit Juli 2024, 558 Strafanträge bis Ende Juli 2026. Hinweis: die Seite trägt in den Metadaten das Datum 2024-11-21, der Text ist von September 2026 (Datum aus OTS übernommen).

name: Geneva rejects new body to monitor Airbnb rentals
text: Swissinfo, 6 Nov 2026 (translated from French): on Thursday the Geneva cantonal parliament amended Marc Saudan's motion, saying a new IT system is enough, and passed it 65 to 31 with one abstention. The original asked for a register of all short-term lets, a supervisory body and a report in six months; the amendment kept only an assessment report within 12 months. Planned regulatory changes: registration of foreign guests for all accommodation providers, an official registration number displayed by booking platforms, and an alert to the cantonal housing office and commercial police at the 90-night limit. Funding approved per Nicolas Walder. 90-day primary-residence limit upheld by the Federal Court.

name: Airbnb will mit Hotelbuchungen Milliardenumsaetze erzielen
text: Tageskarte (9 Nov 2026), based on Airbnb's Q3 2026 call of 5 Nov: Chesky expects billions in hotel revenue in coming years but gave no formal forecast or timeline. Hotel pilot began in four cities; now thousands of boutique and independent hotels in 60+ destinations. Chesky puts the global hotel market at about 900 billion dollars. Airbnb reaches many Gen Z and upscale travellers; hotels value presentation, extra audience and international reach. About 35% of guests whose first booking is a hotel book a vacation home within a year. Pepijn Rijvers (ex Booking.com, responsible there for all accommodation) joined in September as Chief Business Officer for homes, hotels and international expansion. Airbnb gave no hotel revenue, growth rates or commission/terms for hotels.

Customers: banks, airlines, OTAs, travel tech, publishers. name: Who Would Pay Costa Rica's Proposed 10% Tax on Airbnb Platforms
text: Tico Times, 23 Nov 2026: A bill signed by Frente Amplio deputy José María Villalta Flórez-Estrada and six colleagues would levy a special 10% charge on commissions and service fees of short-stay platforms for properties in Costa Rica, wherever the company is domiciled. At a 15% platform commission the tax equals 1.5% of the booking if passed on; the consumer group Asociación de Consumidores Libres (president Juan Ricardo Fernández) expects guests to bear it on top of 13% VAT and calls it protectionism. Revenue split: 50% municipalities, 30% Banhvi, 20% ICT. Municipalities could cap short-term rentals per district, neighbourhood or building given technical studies; single-unit owners need seven requirements to register with the ICT; fines up to 20 base salaries (about 9.2m colones, $20,600); platforms must hand host and guest data to state institutions. The bill cannot advance until the Executive adds it to the agenda of extraordinary sessions (running since 1 Nov); months away at earliest. Bill number 25.910 per the editor's brief is not stated in the text.

Partners get ready-made booking sites, system access (API) or branded travel deals, with 4.7m+ properties, 500+ airlines and 200+ car rental firms. Per CNBC, Booking bets on the larger unit to drive growth as AI changes trip booking; a travel-focused AI agent for partners is planned without a launch date. name: 'Autonomy is earned': how Dwelly's AI took over half of letting steps
text: TNW (23 Nov 2026): Dwelly, a UK roll-up of letting agencies (20 agencies, 13 bought in 2026; 17,000+ properties; ~$470m annual rent; $263m raised incl. $170m round in July; ~300 staff), says its AI agents, rolled out from April 2026, complete about 55% of letting steps with no human (September estimate). Manual touches per letting fell from 28 to ~25 flagged items (about half one-click approvals, ~13 real work). Answered within an hour: 35% to ~90%; offer to paid holding deposit 5 to 2.4 days; fall-throughs 14% to 9%; negotiator time per letting 6.5h to 3.2h; negotiator portfolio 350 to ~700 capacity (now ~386, target 1,000+); managers 100 to 300+ units. AI answers two-thirds of landlord calls. Built on Anthropic Claude and OpenAI via business APIs on UK-hosted infrastructure. Targets Q1 2027: 85% of steps autonomous, five manual touches, six days offer to signed (19 before April, ~11 now). Co-founder/CPO is Dan Lifshits.

name: EU opens Digital Services Act investigation into Booking.com over scams
text: The Next Web (Ana-Maria Stanciuc): the Commission opened its first formal DSA investigation into Booking.com, announced Wednesday 21 October 2026, on three areas: fake listings, protection of reservation and guest data shared with hosts (phishing), and labelling of paid-for higher-ranked listings. Booking.com reports over 45 million monthly EU users; fines up to 6% of annual global turnover; no fixed deadline; commitments possible. Booking.com says it is cooperating fully. Context: Meta DSA scam-ads probe since 2024, X fined EUR 120 million.

name: What Happened in the Vienna State Parliament? These Five Topics Are Important
text: VIENNA.at, 21.10.2026: Der Wiener Landtag debattierte am Dienstag (20.10.) fast 14 Stunden (9:00 bis 22:44). Beschlossen wurden Änderungen der Bauordnung und die Regeln für ein neues Kurzzeitvermietungsregister, mit den Stimmen von SPÖ, NEOS, FPÖ und Grünen; die ÖVP stimmte nicht zu. Plattformen müssen prüfen, ob eine Unterkunft registriert ist, und Angebote ohne gültige Nummer entfernen. Die technische Umsetzung des Registers hängt aber noch von einer Schnittstelle des Bundes ab. Weitere Themen: Mindestsicherung (nicht beschlossen), Verkürzung der Budget-Auflage von vier auf zwei Wochen, Kinder- und Jugendhilfe, Hitzeschutz an Schulen.

name: About the pay-per-booking (PPB) model
text: Vrbo Help Center page (primary source; the 2026-01-01 date is a page-date placeholder, the text reflects the post-29-Oct-2026 model). Under pay-per-booking Vrbo charges 12% on the rental amount plus host-charged fees such as cleaning, pet and boat fees. No commission on Vrbo traveler service fees, taxes, refundable deposits or insurance. With Vrbo's merchant-of-record service, the 12% is all-in with no separate processing fee; hosts with their own processor pay 12% plus that processor's fees. In some regions (parts of Europe, Australia, New Zealand) hosts on the Professional Plan may pay up to 15% including processing. VAT is added where it applies; in Australia, Japan and New Zealand 12% plus GST rules apply (Australia 0.5%, NZ 0.75% effective GST on commission).

name: Wiener Landtag, 15. Sitzung vom 20.10.2026, Wörtliches Protokoll, Seite 121
text: Wörtliches Protokoll des Wiener Landtags, 20.10.2026, Seite 121 von 126. Eine NEOS-Rednerin erklärt, der Landtag beschliesse 'heute zwei Gesetze': das Wiener Register zur Kurzzeitvermietung und eine Bauordnungsnovelle. Das Register setze eine EU-Verordnung um; alle auf Plattformen angebotenen Wohnungen erhalten eine Registrierungsnummer, Vermieter und Plattformen sind zur Registrierung bzw. Prüfung verpflichtet. Die Bauordnung soll Umwidmungen von Wohnungen in Beherbergungsstätten verhindern; 20 Prozent der Nutzfläche bleiben umwidmbar, die 90-Tage-Regel bleibt.

name: Wiener Landtag, 15. Sitzung vom 20.10.2026, Wörtliches Protokoll, Seite 125
text: Wörtliches Protokoll des Wiener Landtags, 20.10.2026, Seite 125 von 126. Eine SPÖ-Rednerin (Abg. Seidl) erläutert den Antrag: Umwandlung in Beherbergungsstätten erschwert, Ausnahmen-Lücken geschlossen, Mindeststrafen, Wiener Kurzzeitvermietungsregister mit Registrierungsnummer; Plattformen wie Airbnb oder booking.com müssen Angebote ohne Nummer unterbinden und Daten mit der Stadt teilen. Wien sei österreichweit die erste Stadt mit so einem Register; früher ging es nicht, weil der Bund erst die technische Schnittstelle schafft. Danach schliesst der Präsident die Verhandlung.

name: Wiener Landtag, 15. Sitzung vom 20.10.2026, Wörtliches Protokoll, Seite 126

history.why: Der Markt ist fragmentiert, Funding ist knapper, Konsolidierung in Hospitality-Software ist ein wiederkehrendes Muster. Startwert, wird mit Belegen angepasst.
